layout_details.content: 1) The International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) is a worldwide organization for standardization comprising all national electrotechnical committees (IEC National Committees). The object of IEC is to promote international co-operation on all questions concerning standardization in the electrical and electronic fields. To this end and in addition to other activities, IEC publishes International Standards, Technical Specifications, Technical Reports, Publicly Available Specifications (PAS) and Guides (hereafter referred to as "IEC Publication(s)"). Their preparation is entrusted to technical committees; any IEC National Committee interested in the subject dealt with may participate in this preparatory work. International, governmental and nongovernmental organizations liaising with the IEC also participate in this preparation. IEC collaborates closely with the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) in accordance with conditions determined by agreement between the two organizations.

layout_details.content: This fourth edition cancels and replaces the third edition published in 2009. This edition constitutes a technical revision.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - support of advanced constructs such as
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - conditions and constraints,
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - blocks,
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - cardinality,
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - polymorphism,
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - generic and restricted enumerations, and
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - mapping;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - extended list of data types;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - harmonization with IEC 62656-1;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - support of IEC TS 62720 and of coded units;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - harmonization of semantic and administrative data among the various information objects;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # INTRODUCTION
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The IEC 61360 series as a whole specifies a general purpose dictionary of technical terms covering the field of electrotechnology, electronics and related domains. The dictionary is specified in a computer-sensible form as a reference dictionary. By using the dictionary, applications can interact and share data in an unambiguous way free from semantic uncertainties.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: This document addresses domain engineers and provides a detailed introduction to the structure of the dictionary and its uses from the viewpoint of the dictionary provider as well as from the viewpoint of the user of the dictionary. IEC 61360-2 specifies the detailed dictionary data model and IEC 61360-6 stipulates quality criteria for the content of the dictionary.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Referencing to a common dictionary is advantageous in all cases where product information has to be transferred in an unambiguous way. Use cases include catalogues, ordering processes, product information contained in specifications or contracts.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The International Electrotechnical Commission has set up a technical dictionary for the use in the electrotechnical and electronic domain which is maintained by SC 3D. This dictionary is called IEC Common Data Dictionary (IEC CDD) and can be accessed on the following IEC web page: http://std.iec.ch/iec61360.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Dictionaries should not be confused with catalogues or master data collections; these make use of dictionary objects. In catalogues or master data collections, values are assigned to instances of dictionary objects. Thus they build upon dictionaries. Consequently, dictionaries are normally exchanged in advance of any catalogue or master data.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Closely associated with this document is IEC 61360-2, which contains the information model using the EXPRESS modelling language. In this model, the definition and structure of IEC 61360-1 is formalized and presented in a computer-sensible form.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: This document is largely compliant with IEC 61360-2:2012 and ISO 13584-42:2010. However, practical use has shown the necessity to selectively extend the data model. Thus, this fourth edition of IEC 61360-1 extends IEC 61360-2 in both semantics and syntax and introduces additional constructs available from IEC 62656-1 for practical benefits. For example, constructs such as enumerations of real numbers or relation objects do not exist in IEC 61360-2, but are needed in many fields of engineering.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: IEC 62656-1 provides interfaces to IEC CDD. Thus, change requests to IEC CDD need to be formed according to the interface specification available from the latter standard.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In some cases it can be difficult to see whether words represent names of information objects or if just everyday items are addressed, e.g. by the term "property".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For this reason, the following typographic rules are used in this document:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - bold, upper case first letter: name of a UML class, e.g. "Property";
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - bold, lower case first letter: name of a UML attribute or UML association, e.g. "revision_number";
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - normal font (i.e. not bold), lower case first letter: floating text, e.g. "property".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: UML information object names should be treated as constants and should not be translated in other languages.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # STANDARD DATA ELEMENT TYPES WITH ASSOCIATED CLASSIFICATION SCHEME Part 1: Definitions - Principles and methods
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 1 Scope
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: This part of IEC 61360 specifies principles for the definition of the properties and associated attributes and explains the methods for representing verbally defined concepts with appropriate data constructs available from IEC 61360-2. It also specifies principles for establishing a hierarchy of classification from a collection of classes, each of which represents a technical concept in the electrotechnical domain or a domain related to electrotechnology.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The use of this document facilitates the exchange of technical data through a defined structure for the information to be exchanged in a computer-sensible form. Each property to be exchanged has an unambiguously defined meaning and consistent naming, where relevant a defined value list, a prescribed format and defined units of measure for all quantitative values. There is also provision for:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) control of changes to definitions of the properties through version and revision numbers;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) inclusion of notes and remarks to clarify and help in the application of the definitions;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) indication of the sources of definitions and value lists;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: d) associated figures and formulae.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE IEC TCs and SCs, or other organizations can take this document as a basis for the development of their own dictionaries.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Out of scope of this document are subjects concerning the information technology infrastructure such as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - security;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - database locking mechanisms;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - access rights management.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 4 Foundation for the concepts of IEC 61360 standard dictionaries
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In the IEC 61360 series, the basic concepts underlying the full data model are those of "dictionary", "class", and "property".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The concept of a product is captured by entities called "classes" and its characteristics are captured by entities called "properties". A hierarchy of classes in this document is an ordering of classes according to the commonalities of the properties in the classes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The following clauses provide details on these concepts and their interrelations.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: To show the concepts Unified Modelling Language (UML, see ISO/IEC 19505-1) class diagrams are used in Clauses 6 to 23. Clause 24 uses a spreadsheet-based presentation introduced by IEC 62656-1:2014 for representing structures containing instances.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 The UML models are for explanatory purposes; a detailed data model for implementation is given in IEC 61360-2.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 1 shows a simplified overview model of the IEC 61360-1 information objects and their interrelations.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 1 - Simplified model of IEC 61360-1 (UML class diagram)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 The association enumeration of Figure 1 is implemented via the enumeration data types.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The IEC 61360 dictionary model has a single inheritance model. However, from time to time, some properties defined in another class which resides in other branches of specialization hierarchy become necessary and pertinent.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In this case, the model offers the case-of mechanism to import properties of a fixed version (see 24.3). Once imported into a class, such properties become applicable in the class and inherited into its subclasses as applicable properties. The importation of properties is achieved by listing the properties to be imported in the "imported_properties" attribute of the case-of class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note that once a case-of relationship is installed, the version of the imported property is fixed, and even if the definition of the property is changed in the source class, the imported property does not change.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: See Annex A for the detailed UML class diagrams of IEC 61360-1. Annex H gives a short introduction of the used UML constructs.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Annex C provides advice on preparation of new classes and properties.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5 Dictionary identification
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The IEC Common Data Dictionary (IEC CDD) contains a collection of classes and properties. All information objects in a dictionary are uniquely identified including a version identifier as a record of significant changes to a dictionary object. This enables a version control for each dictionary object. And the identification of a dictionary object is therefore not dependent on a publication of the whole dictionary at a particular point in time.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For use of the dictionary content in communication it can be helpful to identify the complete set of dictionary items with a reference. For this reason the IEC CDD as a whole is identified by the following attributes given in 5.2 to 5.6.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.2 Dictionary_supplier
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: dictionary_supplier
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: identification of any organization authorized to register dictionary items
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: The identifier is specified in ISO 13584-26:2000. The source identification for the IEC 61360-4 reference dictionary is: "0112/2//61360_4".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Other sources may require different identifications.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 The source identification of the standard does not include an edition number contrary to what ISO 13584-26:2000 has defined.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 The hyphen "-" in "61360-4" is replaced by an underscore "_".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE "0112/2///61987" is the source identification for data of IEC 61987 series.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: mandatory
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: String constant as specified
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 3 The slash "/" separator is used in a physical file in accordance with ISO 10303-21. In other environments such as XML other separators can be used.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.3 Code
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: code
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: unique identifier of the dictionary item
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: The content of code for the IEC Common Data Dictionary shall be: "IEC CDD".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: mandatory
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: String constant as specified
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.4 Version_number
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: version_number
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: number used to control the versions of the IEC Common Data Dictionary
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: The version_number of the dictionary should consist of 6 digits. Although the common ISO/IEC EXPRESS information model allows more digits, for the dictionary to be registered into IEC CDD or to be compatible with IEC 61360 series only 6 digits should be used. For specific purposes, version numbers with more digits may be used. Consecutive version numbers starting from "000001" shall be issued in ascending order.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A new version of the dictionary may be generated if at least one class or property is added or when changes are made affecting their version number. When a new version of the dictionary is issued, this data set contains all changes that happened since publication of the last version.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE Intermediate changes of the dictionary can be traced by checking the attribute date_of_current_version.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: mandatory
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: Digits "0" through "9".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.5 Date_of_current_version
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: date_of_current_version
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: date associated with the present content of the IEC Common Data Dictionary
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: The date information of the dictionary shall consist of 10 digits and shall follow the format "YYYY-MM-DD" as specified in ISO 8601:2004.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Whenever the content of the dictionary is modified, the value of the attribute shall be updated.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: mandatory
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: Digits "0" through "9" and "-".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6 Revision_number
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: revision_number
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: number used for administrative control of the IEC Common Data Dictionary
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: The revision_number of the dictionary should consist of 3 digits. Although the common ISO/IEC EXPRESS information model allows more digits, for the dictionary to be registered into IEC CDD or to be compatible with IEC 61360 series only 3 digits should be used. For specific purposes, revision numbers with more digits may be used. Consecutive revision numbers starting from "000" shall be issued in ascending order. Only one revision_number of the dictionary, unique by its identifier, is current at any moment.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A new revision_number of the dictionary shall be generated if an attribute of a dictionary object is changed which neither affects the use, nor the meaning of the dictionary objects.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE Editorial changes such as correction of typing errors.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The content of revision_number shall be reset to the starting value "1" when the version_number is incremented
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: mandatory
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: Digits "0" through "9".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 6 Property
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 6.1 Overview
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A property is a characteristic of an object such as a component (see 3.1.24, Note 1). A property, when used, always has an associated value, such as a numerical value together with a unit, or a qualitative value taken from a predefined list.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In Clause 6, the various attributes of properties as encountered in the specifications are explained. For a list of these attributes, see Table 2. These attributes are related to identification, description, value of characteristics and to its relationships.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: When specifying properties and their associated data type care, should be taken that the anticipated value is meaningful. In particular, the use of BOOLEAN_TYPE values may lead to deficient specifications if the meaning of the values "TRUE" and "FALSE" is not properly specified. In many cases the use of a value list instead of Boolean values provides more precise information and should be preferred.

layout_details.content: ## 7 Identifying_attributes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 7.1 Overview
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The Identifying_attributes information object collects the attributes specifying the identity of an information object.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: To identify an information object uniquely a language independent combination of characters shall be used. The identifier shall consist of the six-character code, followed by a hyphen followed by the three-digit version number of the information object.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For ensuring the global uniqueness of the identifiers in the reference dictionary the identification of the registration authority should be added to the identifier. The registration authority identification concept is defined in ISO/IEC 6523-1. At first, an organization identification scheme is selected from the registered schemes using the International Code Designator (ICD). Then, within this scheme, the organization is identified with the Organization Identifier (OI) (see Table 3).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For the IEC Common Data Dictionary, the ICD code "0112" shall be used standing for "Registration of Standardization Organization". For the Organization Identifier (OI), number "2" shall be used standing for "IEC".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A source identification for the data in IEC Common Data Dictionary is: "0112/2//61360_4". The added "61360_4" at the end is the Standards Identifier (SI) which is described in ISO 13584-26 as an extension to ISO/IEC 6523-1.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The IEC Common Data Dictionary may comprise multiple collections of dictionary items. Such collections do not create new identification spaces, i.e. identifiers shall be unique within the whole address space.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 The globally unique identification of a particular information object can be "0112/2///61340_4#AAF307#005".
layout_details.label: text

A new revision of an information object shall be generated if an attribute of the information object is changed which neither affects its use nor its meaning, or when corrections of typing or spelling errors have been implemented.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The revision_number shall be reset to its starting value "000" when the version_number is changed.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: See Annex D for rules for defining new versions or revisions of dictionary elements.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: mandatory
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: Digits "0" through "9".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 7.6 Short_name
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: short_name
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: shortened representation of the content of preferred_name
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: The first character of the content of short_name shall be a letter:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - the short name should be preceded by a "@" character for a Condition_property;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - the short name shall be a short representation of the content in preferred_name. The length of the short name should be limited to 18 characters.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: optional
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: See Clause 26.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 7.7 Synonymous_name
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: synonymous_name
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: single-word or multi-word designation that differs from the given preferred name but represents the same concept
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: The number of synonymous names shall be limited to two. For pragmatic reasons, the length of the synonymous_name should be limited to 70 characters.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: optional
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: See Clause 26.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 7.8 Version_number
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: version_number
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: number used to control the versions of an information object
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: The version_number of an information object should consist of 3 digits. Although the common ISO/IEC EXPRESS information model allows more digits, for the information object to be registered into IEC CDD or to be compatible with IEC 61360 series only 3 digits should be used. For specific purposes, version numbers with more digits may be used. Consecutive version numbers starting from "001" shall be issued in ascending order. Per information object, unique by its identifier, only one version number is current at any time.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A new version of an information object shall be generated if at least one attribute of the information object has changed which can affect its use but which does not affect its meaning.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: See Annex D for rules for defining new versions or revisions of dictionary elements.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: mandatory
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: Digits "0" through "9".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 8 Semantic_attributes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 8.1 Overview
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The Semantic_attributes information object collects the attributes specifying the meaning of an information object.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 8.2 Specification of information object
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Name: Semantic_attributes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Definition: collection of attributes specifying the semantic content of an information object
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 5 shows the detailed model of the information object "Semantic_attributes" using UML as presentation technique.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 5 - Semantic attributes (UML class diagram)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 8.3 Definition
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: definition
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: on: statement that describes the meaning of an information object in an unambiguous and unique manner to permit its differentiation from other information objects
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 Definition of "arcing distance": arcing distance value of the shortest distance in air external to the insulator between metallic parts normally having the operating voltage between them
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: Conventions and requirements:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE An information object standardized under former editions of IEC 61360-1 can be updated only by initiating a change request.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) The content of definition of an information object shall be derived from the original definition as appearing in the latest corresponding IEC or ISO standards, if available.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) Where possible, definitions of property information objects shall be independent from classes. Thus, reuse of properties as part of other class information objects is supported.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) ISO 704 should be used as a basis for the writing of the definition statement.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: d) The unit of measure shall not be included in the definition statement.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: e) The level information should not occur in the definition statement.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE Level information can be specified with the data type level_type.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: f) The semantic context should be included in the definition statement, if this is essential for the understanding of its meaning.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: g) If the concept requires a limitation of its applicability, this shall be explicitly expressed in the definition statement.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 There exist different semantics of the term "rated voltage"; within products $ \geq1, 5 \mathrm{kV} $ , the term rated voltage expresses the maximum voltage for which a product is being designed and can be operated. This is currently not applicable to products less than 1,5 kV.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: h) If dependency relations are an inherent part of the concept, these shall be included in the definition statement.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 3 Definition statement of the Property "reverse recovery time":
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: "value of the time required for the reverse current of a diode to recover to a specified value, when switched from a specified forward current to a specified reverse voltage, at specified conditions"
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: i) In the case conditions are specified, the definition statement should end with the wording "at specified condition(s)".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: j) If the concept represents an average value, the method of calculating the average shall be identified, by using a term that designates the method, such as "arithmetic mean", "geometric mean", "median", or "mode", either in the preferred_name or in the definition.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: See Annex F for conventions for definitions.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: mandatory
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: See Clause 26.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 8.4 Note
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: note
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: statement providing further information on the definition which is considered to be essential for its understanding
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: EXAMPLE The Property "reverse recovery time" is further clarified by a note: "The reverse recovery time is measured as the time interval between $ t_{0} $ the point where the forward current crosses the zero current axis, and the instant when for decreasing values of $ i_{\mathrm{R}} $ a line through the points for 0,9 $ I_{\mathrm{RM}} $ and 0,25 $ I_{\mathrm{RM}} $ crosses the zero current axis."
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: optional
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: See Clause 26.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 8.5 Remark
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: remark
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: additional information in text
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: The content of remark shall not change the meaning of the definition.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: optional
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: See Clause 26.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 8.6 Source_document_of_definition
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: source_document_of_definition
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: reference to the source document from which the content of definition was derived
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: The document shall be recognized by the ISO or IEC committee concerned as having wide acceptance and authoritative status as well as being publicly available.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: optional.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: See Clause 26.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.8 Revision_released_on

layout_details.content: ## 9.9 Status_level
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: status_level
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: name of the stage of the standardization workflow the information object is in
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: The following status levels may be assigned:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Proposal status level of a new information object from its registration and identification in the database, until it has been accepted for work and a resolution has been reached on how to proceed following the preliminaries
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Draft status level of a new information object that has been accepted for work following the preliminaries with either the normal or extended database procedure, until the moment a decision has been taken on whether or not it is to be part of the standard
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 The transition to status_level "draft" is from status_level "proposal".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Standard status level of a new information object that has been released for use as part of the standard
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 The transition to status_level "standard" is from status_level "draft".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Superseded status level of an information object that is no longer part of the standard, irrespective of reason
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 3 The transition to status_level "superseded" is from status_level "standard". On the information object page a note or a reference to a replacing information object further indicates the reason for obsolescence.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Rejected status of an information object that has been entered into the database as part of a change request, but has not been approved to be part of the standard
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 4 The transition to "rejected" is either from status_level "proposal" or from status_level "draft".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: mandatory
layout_details.label: text
