layout_details.content: ## 10 Value_attributes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.1 Overview
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The Value_attributes information object collects the attributes that specify the numerical or non-numerical value of a Property.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Every Property information object may have a value domain that covers the range of permissible values being either implicitly specified by the value_format or explicitly specified by listing the allowed values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For quantitative Property information objects, the value domain may be expressed either as a value range providing the minimum and maximum values or as an explicit enumeration of discrete possible values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For non-quantitative Property information objects, the value domain can be expressed by enumerating the permissible values in the form of text strings.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE The attribute value_format (see 10.8) can be used as an indicator for the intended values that can be assigned to a Property during its usage. Additionally, it can be used for performing a basic quality control on the data provided.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For Property information objects with predefined value sets, a mechanism using values represented by value codes and associated value meanings, is described in Clause 16.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: If a Property serves as classifying property, a value list shall be specified.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.2 Specification of information object
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Name: Value_attributes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Definition: collection of attributes specifying the value(s) and unit(s) of an information object
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 7 shows the detailed model of the information object "Value_attributes" using UML as presentation technique.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
Value_attributes
data_type[1]
value_format[0..1]
unit_of measure[0..1]
alternative_units_of measure[0..*]
referenced_class_identifier[0..1]
number_of_significant_digits[0..1]
layout_details.label: table

layout_details.content: Figure 7 - Value_attributes (UML class diagram)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.3 Alternative_units_of measure
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: alternative_units_of measure
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: units which may be used as an alternative to specify the value of a property
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 Alternative units allow the recommendation of further units in addition to the preferred unit (see 10.7). Reasons to choose an alternative unit are causes such as specific measurement principles, particular application domains, or special legislative systems.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 Alternative units can be made available in purpose-related groups of units (see 24.8.3).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: Conventions and requirements:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) Alternative units may be supplied in addition to a preferred unit. Such alternative units can, but do not have to be, SI units.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE bar, psi, or Torr instead of Pa.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
b) Alternative units may be specified by using the code of the unit as specified in IEC TS 62720 or compliant unit dictionaries.

NOTE 3 The unit dictionaries can be supplied in computer-sensible form or as paper.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) The conversion to a different unit is outside the scope of this document.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
d) It is out of scope of this document to prescribe the use of a specific unit for transaction purposes including possible prefixes.

NOTE 4 Property information objects with data_type "CLASS_REFERENCE_TYPE" do not carry a unit.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: e) It is strongly recommended not to specify the same concept in different properties if only the prefixes of the related units are different. Exceptions may occur if certain units are very common in particular business domains, such as "nm" (nanometre) in semiconductor manufacturing or "kV" (kilovolt) in the power distribution domain.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: f) Each unit contained in the alternative_units_of_measure attribute is required to be associated with a string representation, whose text representation can be used for characterizing the unit at the instance level.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: optional
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: See Clause 26.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.4 Data_type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 0.4.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: data_type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: identifies a specific quality of the value of a Property
layout_details.label: text
text

layout_details.content: Obligation: mandatory
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of value: See Clause 26.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.4.2 Simple type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A data type specifying that the value of a Property is a single numeric or a non-numeric value. The value format shall be defined according to 10.8.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In each designation of type where “_TYPE” is found, “_TYPE” may be omitted.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For a simple type, the valid data types are:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## BOOLEAN_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type BOOLEAN_TYPE may be used for values representing truth values of logic or Boolean algebra or pattern of truth values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The use of "TRUE" as Boolean value indicates a true or accurate result. "FALSE" as Boolean value expresses a wrong or inaccurate result. Other values are deprecated.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 Deprecated Boolean values are values such as "YES" or "NO" and "Y" or "N".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: If a value contains a single truth value the data format shall contain "B1".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 The use of BOOLEAN_TYPE values can lead to deficient specifications if the meaning of the values is not properly specified. In many cases the use of a value list instead of BOOLEAN_TYPE values provides more precise information.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Additionally, some types of presentations can become meaningless if BOOLEAN_TYPE values are used.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 In circuit diagrams, lead texts are often omitted because of space restrictions or avoidance of the need for translation, and only the values are presented. Figure 8 shows examples for technical data associated with connecting lines presented in an abbreviated form (see IEC 61082:2014, Figure 38). In such cases, the use of values of BOOLEAN_TYPE could lead to presentations that are difficult to interpret, as such values are meaningless without lead text.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 8 - Examples for technical data associated with connecting lines
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## BINARY_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type BINARY_TYPE may be used for values containing a sequence of bits, each bit being represented by "0" or "1". The value format shall be "Bn" with n > 1. The textual part of the property, i.e. content of the attributes "definition", "note" or "remark", should give guidance about the interpretation of the bit pattern.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 There is no upper limit specified for the value of "n". Current implementations (in 2014) support sequences of bits ("bitstrings") of a size up to 2 gigabytes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## STRING_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type STRING_TYPE may be used for values containing any sequence of elements, typically characters, using some character encoding.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Instead of the STRING_TYPE one of the more specific data types may be used:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - TRANSLATABLE_STRING_TYPE;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - NON_TRANSLATABLE_STRING_TYPE;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - NON_QUANTITATIVE_CODE_TYPE (deprecated);
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - DATE_TIME_TYPE;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - DATE_TYPE;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - TIME_TYPE;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - IRDI_STRING;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - URI_TYPE.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - HTML5_TYPE.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## TRANSLATABLE_STRING_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type TRANSLATABLE_STRING_TYPE may be used for values containing strings, but that are supposed to be represented as different strings in different languages.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## NON_TRANSLATABLE_STRING_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type NON_TRANSLATABLE_STRING_TYPE may be used for values containing strings but that shall be represented in the same way in any language, i.e. such strings shall not be translated.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 3 The MAC address of a computer, e.g. "00-80-41-ae-fd-7e".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## DATE_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type DATE_TYPE may be used for values containing a calendar date specified according to a representation compliant with ISO 8601.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A value whose data type is DATE_TYPE shall comply with the following lexical representation, which is a subset of the lexical representations allowed by ISO 8601. The lexical representation for DATE_TYPE is the reduced (right truncated) lexical representation for DATE_TIME_TYPE: "YYYY-MM-DD". No left truncation is allowed. An optional following time zone qualifier is allowed as for DATE_TIME_TYPE. To accommodate year values outside the range from "0001" to "9999", additional digits may be added to the left of this representation and a preceding "-" sign is allowed.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 4 "1999-05-31" is the DATE_TYPE representation of: "31 May 1999".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute format should contain the value "M..10".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## TIME_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type TIME_TYPE may be used for values defining a time specified according to a representation compliant with ISO 8601. A value of TIME_TYPE represents an instant of time that recurs every day.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 Only a subset of the lexical representations allowed by ISO 8601 is allowed for values of TIME_TYPE.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 3 The above restriction of ISO 8601 representations is the same as the one defined by XML Schema.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 4 Since the lexical representation allows an optional time zone indicator, TIME_TYPE values are partially ordered because it is not possible to determine the order of two values one of which has a time zone and the other does not.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A value whose data type is TIME_TYPE shall comply with the following lexical representation, which is a subset of the lexical representations allowed by ISO 8601. The lexical representation for TIME_TYPE is the left truncated lexical representation for DATE_TIME_TYPE "hh:mm:ss.sss" with optional following time zone indicator.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 5 "13:20:00-05:00" is the TIME_TYPE representation of: 1.20 p.m. for Eastern Standard Time which is 5 hours behind Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute format should contain the value "M..14".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## DATE_TIME_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type DATE_TIME_TYPE may be used for values defining an instant of time specified according to a particular representation compliant with ISO 8601.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A value whose data type is DATE_TIME_TYPE shall comply with the following lexical representation, which is a subset of the lexical representations allowed by ISO 8601. This lexical representation is the ISO 8601 extended format "YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss" where "YYYY" represents the year, "MM" the month and "DD" the day, preceded by an optional leading "-" sign. The letter "T" is the date/time separator and "hh", "mm", "ss" represent hour, minute and second, respectively. Additional digits can be used to increase the precision of fractional seconds if desired, i.e. the format "ss.ss..." with any number of digits after the decimal point is supported. The fractional second part is optional; other parts of the lexical form are not optional. To accommodate year values greater than "9999" additional digits can be added to the left of this representation. Leading zeros are required if the year value would otherwise have fewer than four digits; otherwise they are forbidden. The year "0000" is prohibited. The "YYYY" field shall have at least four digits, the "MM", "DD", "SS", "hh", "mm" and "ss" fields exactly two digits each (not counting fractional seconds); leading zeroes shall be used if the field would otherwise have too few digits. This representation may be immediately followed by a "Z" to indicate "Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)" or, to indicate the time zone, i.e. the difference between the local time and Coordinated Universal Time, immediately followed by a sign, "+" or "-", followed by the difference from UTC represented as "hh:mm". If the time zone is included, both hours and minutes shall be present.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ISO 8601 provides details about legal values in the various fields. If the time zone is included, both hours and minutes shall be present.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 6 To indicate 1:20 p.m. on 31 May 1999 for Eastern Standard Time which is 5 hours behind Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), one would write: "1999-05-31T13:20:00-05:00".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 5 The above restriction of ISO 8601 representations is the same as the one defined by XML Schema.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute format should contain the value "M..25".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## IRDI_STRING_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type IRDI_STRING_TYPE may be used for values conforming to ISO/IEC 11179 series global identifier sequences.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: IRDI, DI and code have the following relationship:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: IRDI::= RAI'#'DI'#'VI
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 6 RAI stands for the registration authority identifier, DI for the data identifier, and VI for the version identifier. Code attribute is used as DI in this document.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 7 In implementation, a data validation can be applied to check whether an information object exists for the referenced IRDI code.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: IRDI_STRING_TYPE may be used instead of one of the more specific data types:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ICID_STRING_TYPE;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ISO_29002_IRDI.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ICID_STRING_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type ICID_STRING_TYPE may be used for values conforming to IRDI_STRING_TYPE, where the delimiter between RAI and DI is "#" while the delimiter between DI and VI is confined to "##".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ICID, DI and code have the following relationship:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ICID::= RAI'#'DI'##'VI
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 8 RAI stands for the registration authority identifier, DI for the data identifier, and VI for the version identifier. Code attribute is used as DI in this document.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 9 In implementation, a data validation can be applied to check whether an information object exists for the referenced ICID code.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ISO_29002_IRDI_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type ISO_29002_IRDI_TYPE may be used for values containing a global identifier that identifies an administrated item in a registry. The structure of this identifier complies with identifier syntax defined in ISO/TS 29002-5. The identifier shall fulfill the requirements specified in ISO/TS 29002-5 for an "international registration data identifier" (IRDI).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: IRDI, DI and code have the following relationship:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: IRDI::= RAI'#'DI'#'VI
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 10 RAI stands for the registration authority identifier, DI for the data identifier, and VI for the version identifier. Code attribute is used as DI in this document.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: As specified in ISO/TS 29002-5, the length of the identifier string shall not be greater than 290 characters.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 11 According to ISO/TS 29002-5 an IRDI consists either of a string that does not contain the '#' character, to identify an organization, or of three sub-strings that do not contain the '#' character and that are separated by the '#' character to identify any other administrated item.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 12 If IRDI is not used for identifying an organization:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - the first sub-string, called the "Registration Authority Identifier (RAI)", identifies the organization which is responsible for the administration of the administrated item;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - the second sub-string, called the "Data Identifier (DI)", contains both a categorization of the administrated item, represented by two characters followed by the minus ("-") sign as defined in ISO/TS 29002-5 (e.g. "class", "property", "unit"), and the identifier assigned to the administrated item by the RAI;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - the third sub-string corresponds to the "Version Identifier (VI)" of the IRDI.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## URI_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type URI_TYPE may be used for values containing any sequence of characters that is a URI.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 13 A URI_type allows in particular to express a URL.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## HTML5_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type HTML5_TYPE may be used for values containing strings with any sequence of characters, using the syntax of HTML5 (see W3C Recommendation 28:2014). This content provides for a pictorial presentation that can be impossible to achieve by solely using characters.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 14 As HTML5 supports MathML (see W3C Recommendation 10:2014), mathematical formulas can be presented.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 7 The value $ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} $ 420kV (242,48711305964282109384248781082 kV) can be expressed with
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: HTML5_TYPE as
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<!doctype html>

<html>

  <head>

    <meta charset="UTF-8">

  </head>

  <body>

    <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">

      <mrow>

        <mrow>

          <mfrac>

            <mn>1</mn>

            <msqrt>

              <mn>3</mn>

            </msqrt>

          </mfrac>

        </mrow>

        <mo>·</mo>

        <mn>420</mn>

        <mi>kV</mi>

      </mrow>

    </math>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

</body>

</html>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Cases exist where, in addition to the presentation of the value, its exact numeric value is of interest too. In such cases reference to an Item_class is recommended that provides a Property for the numeric value (data type INTEGER, REAL, etc.) and a Property for the HTML presentation (data type HTML5).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 15 The class is referenced by using CLASS_INSTANCE_REFERENCE.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## NUMBER_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type NUMBER_TYPE may be used for values containing numbers that can be written as numeric values. This data type may be used when a more specific numeric representation is not important or unwanted.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Instead of the NUMBER_TYPE one of the more specific data types may be used:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - INTEGER;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - RATIONAL;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: REAL.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## INTEGER, INT_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type INT_TYPE may be used for values containing numbers that can be written as positive or negative whole numbers or as zero.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Instead of the INT_TYPE one of the more specific data types may be used:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - INT_MEASURE_TYPE;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - INT_CURRENCY_TYPE.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## INT_MEASURE_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type INT_MEASURE_TYPE may be used for values containing values that are measures of type INTEGER.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In addition, the data type specifies a unit or a unit identifier, in which the values are expressed. It may also specify alternative units or alternative unit identifiers that are valid if the value is explicitly associated with one of these units.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Either a unit or a unit identifier is mandatory. In cases where both are provided, the unit takes precedence.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 16 The unit identifier used in code_of_unit, code_of_alternative_unit, or code_of_list_of_units attributes can resolve to a unit provided by a server for units of measure.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## INT_CURRENCY_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type INT_CURRENCY_TYPE may be used for values containing values that are integer currencies.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## RATIONAL_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type RATIONAL_TYPE may be used for values containing values that are of type rational.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 8 $ \frac{1}{2}, $ $ \frac{3}{4} $ or $ \frac{7}{2} $ are values that can be represented with RATIONAL_TYPE.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Instead of the RATIONAL_TYPE the more specific data type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - RATIONAL_MEASURE_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: may be used.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## RATIONAL_MEASURE_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type RATIONAL_MEASURE_TYPE may be used for values containing values that are measures of type RATIONAL.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 9 A very common diameter for water pipes is " $ \frac{3}{4} $ inch".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In addition, the data type specifies a unit or a unit identifier, in which the values are expressed. It may also specify alternative units or alternative unit identifiers that are valid if the value is explicitly associated with one of these units.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Either a unit or a unit identifier is mandatory. In cases where both are provided, the unit takes precedence.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 17 The unit identifier used in code_of_unit, code_of_alternative_unit, or code_of_list_of_units attributes can resolve to a unit provided by a server for units of measure.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## REAL_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type REAL_TYPE may be used for values containing numbers that can be written as a terminating or non-terminating decimal; a rational or irrational number.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Instead of the REAL_TYPE, one of the more specific data types may be used:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - REAL_MEASURE_TYPE;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - REAL_CURRENCY_TYPE.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## REAL_MEASURE_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type REAL_MEASURE_TYPE may be used for values containing values that are measures of type REAL.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In addition, the data type specifies a unit or a unit identifier in which the values are expressed. It may also specify alternative units or alternative unit identifiers that are valid if the value is explicitly associated with one of these units.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Either a unit or a unit identifier is mandatory. In cases where both are provided, the unit takes precedence.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 18 The unit identifier used in code_of_unit, code_of_alternative_unit, or code_of_list_of_units attributes can resolve to a unit provided by a server for units of measure.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## REAL_CURRENCY_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Data type containing real values of currencies.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.4.3 Enumeration type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The enumeration types may be used for specifying that the content of a value shall be taken from a predefined set of values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In each designation of type where “_TYPE” is found, “_TYPE” may be omitted.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For an enumeration type, the valid data types are:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## ENUM_CODE_TYPE(enum_id), ENUM_CODE_TYPE(enum_id(code1, code2, ...))
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type ENUM_CODE_TYPE may be used for values referencing a set of strings or numerals, as values, each representing assigned meanings.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 enum_id is a global identifier for the enumeration list.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 code1, code2, ... are the value codes of enumerated values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## ENUM_INT_TYPE(enum_id), ENUM_INT_TYPE(enum_id(code1, code2, ...))
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type ENUM_INT_TYPE may be used for values referencing a set of integer values as values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 3 enum_id is a global identifier for the enumeration list.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 4 code1, code2, ... are the value codes of enumerated values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## ENUM_REAL_TYPE(enum_id), ENUM_REAL_TYPE(enum_id(code1, code2, ...))
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type ENUM_REAL_TYPE may be used for values referencing a set of real values as values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 5 enum_id is a global identifier for the enumeration list.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 6 code1, code2, ... are the value codes of enumerated values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 7 "ENUM_REAL_TYPE" is not available in ISO 13584-42/IEC 61360-2, instead a constraint mechanism named "enumeration constraint" can be used for the purpose. However, the specification of the enumeration constraint is much more complex than ENUM_REAL, because the former needs to define first the data type, and then constrain the selectable subset, with an implicit understanding that only one of them is selected.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ENUM_STRING_TYPE(enum_id), ENUM_STRING_TYPE(enum_id(code1, code2, ...))
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type ENUM_STRING_TYPE may be used for values referencing a set of string values, as values, each representing assigned meanings.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 8 "enum_id" is the global identifier of the enumeration list.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 9 "code1", "code2", ... are the codes of the enumerated values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ENUM_RATIONAL_TYPE(enum_id),
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ENUM_RATIONAL_TYPE(enum_id(code1, code2, ...))
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type ENUM_ RATIONAL_TYPE may be used for values referencing a set of string values, as values, each representing a rational number.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 10 "enum_id" is the global identifier of the enumeration list.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 11 "code1", "code2", ... are the codes of the enumerated values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
- ENUM_REFERENCE_TYPE(enum_id), ENUM_INSTANCE_TYPE(enum_id),

  ENUM_REFERENCE_TYPE(enum_id(code1, code2, ...)),

  ENUM_INSTANCE_TYPE(enum_id(code1, code2, ...))
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type ENUM_REFERENCE_TYPE/ ENUM_INSTANCE_TYPE may be used for values referencing a set of string values, as values, each representing the global identifier of a class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 12 "enum_id" is the global identifier of the enumeration list.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 13 "code1", "code2", ... are the codes of the enumerated values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ENUM_BOOLEAN_TYPE(enum_id),
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ENUM_BOOLEAN_TYPE((enum_id(code1, code2, ...))
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type ENUM_BOOLEAN_TYPE may be used for values referencing a set of Boolean values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 14 "enum_id" is the global identifier of the enumeration list.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 15 "code1", "code2", ... are the codes of the enumerated values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.4.4 Class instance type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type CLASS_INSTANCE_TYPE may be used for values containing a reference to an Item_class. The referenced Item_class may reside in any part of the classification hierarchy and contributes a collection of zero, one or more Property information objects. The value of the referencing Property shall contain the code of the referenced Item_class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A CLASS_INSTANCE_TYPE references an Item_class in a way similar to CLASS_REFERENCE_TYPE (see 10.4.5), but unlike the CLASS_REFERENCE_TYPE, instances conforming to the referenced Item_class shall be kept together with the referencing class, i.e. are internal to the instances of the referencing class. This means if there is an Item_class A with instances $ A_{1}, A_{2}, \dots, A_{n} $ ,where $ A_{1} $ references instance $ B_{1} $ of Item_class B, then the instances $ A_{2}, \dots, A_{n} $ of A reference to different instances of B.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In other words, CLASS_INSTANCE_TYPE assumes that each referencing instance $ A_{1}, A_{2}, \dots, A_{n} $ of Item_class A is linked to its "personal" instance of B. Thus, if $ A_{1} $ references $ B_{1} $ and in the referenced Item_class instance $ B_{1} $ , an instance value is changed, the change is not visible from all (other) referencing Item_class instances $ A_{2}, \dots, A_{n}. $
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 The "icid" in CLASS_REFERENCE_TYPE can omit "VI" (version identifier), in this case the class having the specified identifier with the latest version can be referenced.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 See IEC 62656-1 for detailed information on the structure of the global identifier ICID.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.4.5 Class reference type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## CLASS_REFERENCE_TYPE(icid)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type CLASS_REFERENCE_TYPE may be used for values containing a reference to an Item_class. The referenced Item_class may reside in any part of the classification hierarchy and contributes a collection of zero, one or more Property information objects. The value of the referencing Property shall contain the code of the referenced Item_class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: If there are classes $ A_{1}, A_{2}, \dots, A_{n} $ that reference one and the same external item_class information object B, then the instances of $ A_{1}, A_{2}, \dots, A_{n} $ reference to the same instance $ B_{1} $ of B. In other words, CLASS_REFERENCE_TYPE assumes that the instance stored at the side of the referenced item_class B, is shared among all the referencing classes $ A_{1}, A_{2}, \dots, A_{n} $ . Thus, if in the referenced item_class an instance value is changed, the change is visible from all referencing item_class information objects.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 The "icid" in CLASS_REFERENCE_TYPE can omit "VI" (version identifier). In this case the reference to the latest version of the referenced class is made.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 See IEC 62656-1 for detailed information on the structure of the global identifier ICID.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.4.6 Aggregate type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Data type containing collections of two or more values. Individual values within the aggregate can be identified by a numeric index. One-dimensional sets of values may be represented as bag, list, or set. Multi-dimensional sets of values can be expressed as arrays.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The format applicable to each value of the aggregate shall be defined according to 10.4.2.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - BAG(b1,b2)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A BAG data type has as its domain unordered collections of like constituents. The lower and upper bounds, which are integer-valued, define the minimum and maximum number of constituents that can be held in the collection defined by a BAG data type.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Rules and restrictions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) The b1 expression shall be an integer value greater than or equal to zero. It gives the lower bound, which is the minimum number of constituents that can be in a bag. b1 shall not be the indeterminate value ("?").
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) The b2 expression shall be an integer value greater than or equal to b1, or an indeterminate value ("?"). It gives the upper bound, which is the maximum number of constituents that can be in a bag. If this value is indeterminate ("?"), the number of constituents in a bag is not being bounded from above.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) If the boundary specification is omitted, the limits are (0,?).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## LIST(b1, b2)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A LIST data type has as its domain sequences of like constituents. The lower and upper bounds, which are integer-valued, define the minimum and maximum number of constituents that can be held in the collection defined by a LIST data type.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Rules and restrictions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) The b1 expression shall be an integer value greater than or equal to zero. It gives the lower bound, which is the minimum number of constituents that can be in a list. b1 shall not be the indeterminate value ("?").
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) The b2 expression shall be an integer value greater than or equal to b1, or an indeterminate value ("?"). It gives the upper bound, which is the maximum number of
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: constituents that can be in a list. If this value is indeterminate ("?"), the number of constituents in a list is not being bounded from above.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) If the boundary specification is omitted, the limits are (0,?).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## UNIQUE_LIST(b1, b2)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The value has the form of a LIST in which duplicate values shall not occur.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Rules and restrictions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) The rules and restrictions of the LIST data type apply.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) Each constituent in an occurrence of a UNIQUE_LIST data type shall be different from (that is, not instance equal to) every other constituent in the same list.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## SET(b1, b2)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A SET data type has as its domain unordered collections of like constituents. The lower and upper bounds, which are integer-valued, define the minimum and maximum number of constituents that can be held in the collection defined by a SET data type.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Rules and restrictions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) The b1 expression shall be an integer value greater than or equal to zero. It gives the lower bound, which is the minimum number of constituents that can be in a set. b1 shall not be the indeterminate value ("?").
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) The b2 expression shall be an integer value greater than or equal to b1, or an indeterminate value ("?"). It gives the upper bound, which is the maximum number of constituents that can be in a set value of this data type. If this value is indeterminate ("?"), the number of constituents in a set is not being bounded from above.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) If the boundary specification is omitted, the limits are (0,?).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: d) Each constituent in an occurrence of a SET data type shall be different from (that is, not instance equal to) every other constituent in the same set.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## CONSTRAINED_SET(b1, b2, cmn, cx)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The CONSTRAINED_SET data type has as its domain unordered collections of constituents that may be expressed as SET of values of which subsets may be extracted. The sizes of allowed subsets are defined by their minimal and maximal values. If these sizes do not exist, any subset is allowed.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Rules and restrictions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) The rules and restrictions of the SET data type apply.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) The cmn shall be an integer value greater than or equal to zero. It gives the lower bound, which is the minimum number of constituents that may be extracted. cmn shall not be the indeterminate value ("?").
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) The cmx shall be an integer value greater than or equal to cmn, or an indeterminate value ("?"). It gives the upper bound, which is the maximum number of constituents that may be extracted.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## ARRAY(b1, b2)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: An ARRAY data type has as its domain indexed fixed-size collections of like constituents. The lower and upper bounds, which are integer-valued numbers, define the range of index values, and thus the size of each array collection.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Given that m is the lower bound and n is the upper bound, there are exactly n-m+1 constituents in the array. These constituents are indexed by subscripts from m to n inclusive. The bounds may be positive, negative or zero, but shall not be indeterminate ("?"
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Rules and restrictions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) Both values in the bound specification, b1 and b2, shall be integer values. Neither shall contain the indeterminate (?) value.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) b1 gives the lower bound of the array. This shall be the lowest index which is valid for an array value of this data type.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) b2 gives the upper bound of the array. This shall be the highest index which is valid for an array value of this data type.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: d) b1 shall be less than or equal to b2.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## OPTIONAL_ARRAY(b1, b2)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The value has the form of an ARRAY in which indeterminate values ("?"）may occur.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Rules and restrictions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) The rules and restrictions of the ARRAY data type apply.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) An array value of this data type may have the indeterminate value ("?" at one or more index positions.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## UNIQUE_ARRAY(b1, b2)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The value has the form of an ARRAY in which duplicate values shall not occur.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Rules and restrictions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) The rules and restrictions of the ARRAY data type apply.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) Each constituent in the array shall be different from (that is, not instance equal to) every other constituent in the same array.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## UNIQUE_OPTIONAL_ARRAY(b1, b2)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The value has the form of an ARRAY in which duplicate values shall not occur. Indeterminate values ("?"）may occur.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Rules and restrictions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) The rules and restrictions of the ARRAY data type apply.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) An array value of this data type may have the indeterminate value ("?" at one or more index positions.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) Each constituent in an array shall be different from (that is, not instance equal to) every other constituent in the same array value.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.4.7 Level type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## LEVEL_TYPE(MIN,NOM,TYP,MAX)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data type LEVEL_TYPE may be used for values representing up to four variants of a numeric value which may be given as
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - INT_TYPE;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - INT_MEASURE_TYPE;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - REAL_TYPE;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - REAL_MEASURE_TYPE.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - Each variant of this value expresses the number value in a specific role:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - MIN minimum of the value;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - NOM value as designated;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - TYP value as typically present;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - MAX maximum of the value.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: As the interpretation of the level type values relies on the fixed sequence of the levels, all levels specified for a property have to be represented. There is no obligation to fill all levels with values although it is advised to do so for data consistency reasons.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 In the case of having a property which is of the LEVEL_TYPE min/nom/typ/max and
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - only the "MIN" value shall be transmitted, each of the other values should contain a "NIL" value;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - only the "MIN" and "MAX" values shall be transmitted, each of the other values should contain a "NIL" value.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 In the case of having a property which is of the LEVEL_TYPE min/max - expressing a range - only those two values need be provided.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE The separator sign used to separate the values of the defined levels depends on the implementation.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The use of the level type should be restricted to those Property information objects that are applicable in domains where the reporting of multiple values on a single characteristic is recognized as common practice.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 3 Values used in industries such as the electronic component industry.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Limiting values can be expressed by defining a Property specifying the levels "MIN" or "MAX" or both.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 4 A 12 V (nominal) car battery has 6 cells with a typical voltage of about 2,2 V each, giving a typical battery voltage of about 13,5 V. On charge, the voltage can reach a maximum of about 14,5 V but it is considered fully discharged when the voltage falls below a minimum of 12,5 V.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A specific use of LEVEL_TYPE is the concept of limiting values. When the qualification "limiting" is added to a Property, which may be expressed in its definition, the property (together with its value) specifies a threshold beyond which a device incurs damage resulting in permanent unwanted changes of functional or physical characteristics influencing the performance of the device.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 5 In the case of the car battery (see EXAMPLE 4), the limiting maximum value might be specified at a value of 16,5 V.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In the context of the limiting values, the levels "NOM" and "TYP" do not apply.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Aggregates may contain LEVEL_TYPE values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 6 LIST(1,?) OF LEVEL(MIN,NOM,TYP,MAX) OF REAL_MEASURE_TYPE
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.4.8 Large object type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - LOB (location, media_type, media_subtype, content_transfer_encoding)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A large object (LOB) is an information object that is logically stored as a value of a Property but may be physically stored independent (mostly separated) of the Property information object. Large objects typically store large amounts of data.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE Video data, audio data, images, xml data, archives.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A value of type LOB consists of a list of four values:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - location: Specification of the place where the value of the large object may be accessed. This storage location should be specified in a way that all parties, i.e. the writer and the reader(s) of the LOB, can access the data.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - media_type: Specification of the type of the LOB value specified in accordance with the multipurpose internet mail extensions (MIME), Part 1. See IETF RFC 2045:1996.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - media_subtype: Specification of the subtype of the LOB value specified in accordance with the multipurpose internet mail extensions (MIME), Part 2. See IETF RFC 2046:1996.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - content_transfer_encoding: Specification of the character encoding of the LOB value specified in accordance with the multipurpose internet mail extensions (MIME), Part 3. See IETF RFC 2047:1996.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.4.9 Placement type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Data type containing direction information for locating an item with respect to the coordinate system of its geometric context. Placement type values provide the information for setting up the local coordinate system required for locating the item.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 A detailed specification of the mathematical methods used by the placement types can be found in IEC 62656-1 and ISO 10303-42.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 In the case of ISO 10303-42, AXIS1_PLACEMENT, AXIS2_PLACEMENT_2D, AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D inherit the attribute "location" that is of CARTESIAN_POINT type in 2D or 3D space, from the generic geometric entity "placement". In the case of IEC 61360-1, this is achieved by associating a condition type Property of the
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: placement type, i.e. CARTESIAN_POINT, to the geometric shape that uses either one of AXIS1_PLACEMENT_2D AXIS1_PLACEMENT_3D, AXIS2_PLACEMENT_2D, or AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D data types.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## AXIS1_PLACEMENT_2D(ref_dir $ _{X}$, ref_dir $ _{Y}$)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The values specify a reference direction in two-dimensional space for use as line of symmetry for bodies that are line symmetric.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ref_dir $ ^{\mathrm{X}} $ : Component of the direction vector of the reference direction in X direction of the geometric context coordinate system.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ref_dir $ _{Y} $ : Component of the direction vector of the reference direction in Y direction of the geometric context coordinate system.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## AXIS1_PLACEMENT_3D(ref_dir $ _{X}$, ref_dir $ _{Y}$, ref_dir $ _{Z}$)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The values specify a reference direction in three-dimensional space for use as line of symmetry for bodies that are line symmetric.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ref_dir $ ^{\mathrm{X}} $ : Component of the direction vector of the reference direction in X direction of the geometric context coordinate system.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ref_dir $ ^{\mathrm{Y}} $ : Component of the direction vector of the reference direction in Y direction of the geometric context coordinate system.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ref_dir $ _{Z} $ : Component of the direction vector of the reference direction in Z direction of the geometric context coordinate system.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## AXIS2_PLACEMENT_2D(ref_dir $ _{X}$, ref_dir $ _{Y}$)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The values specify the local X axis of the local coordinate system used for locating an item.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ref_dir $ ^{\mathrm{X}} $ : Component of the direction vector of the local X axis in X direction of the geometric context coordinate system.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ref_dir $ ^{\mathrm{Y}} $ : Component of the direction vector of the local X axis in Y direction of the geometric context coordinate system.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D((ref1_dir $ _{X}$, ref1_dir $ _{Y}$, ref1_dir $ _{Z}$), (ref2_dir $ _{X}$, ref2_dir $ _{Y}$, ref2_dir $ _{Z}$))
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The values specify the local Z axis and the direction used to determine the direction of the X axis of the local coordinate system used for locating an item.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ref1_dir $ ^{\mathrm{X}} $ : Component of the direction vector of the local Z axis in X direction of the geometric context coordinate system.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ref1_dir $ ^{\mathrm{Y}} $ : Component of the direction vector of the local Z axis in Y direction of the geometric context coordinate system.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ref1_dir $ \mathcal{Z} $ : Component of the direction vector of the local Z axis in Z direction of the geometric context coordinate system.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ref2_dir $ ^{\mathrm{X}} $ : Component of the direction vector of the direction used to determine the direction of the local X axis in X direction of the geometric context coordinate system.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ref2_dir $ _{Y} $ : Component of the direction vector of the direction used to determine the direction of the local X axis in Y direction of the geometric context coordinate system.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - ref2_dir $ _{Z} $ : Component of the direction vector of the direction used to determine the direction of the local X axis in Z direction of the geometric context coordinate system.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.4.10 Data type dependencies
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.5 Number_of_significant_digits
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: number_of_significant_digits
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: prescription of the precision that shall be obtained when assigning a numerical value to a property
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: Conventions and requirements:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
a) Trailing zeros without a decimal mark indicate lack of significant digits unless a decimal mark is appended.

EXAMPLE 1 "1000" has one significant digit and "1000," has four significant digits.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) All digits (following a non-zero digit) are significant once a decimal mark is used, so trailing zeros located to the right of the decimal mark are to be considered significant. Zeros with significant digits on each side of the decimal mark are also significant.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 "30,4", "34,0", and "3,40" each have three significant digits but "340" has only two significant digits.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
c) Leading zeros are not treated as significant.

EXAMPLE 3 One or more leading zeroes are not treated as significant,

e.g. 00257,7 has 4 significant digits, and 0,00492 has 6 significant digits.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
d) The sign of the number is independent and is not counted within the significant digits.

EXAMPLE 4 +30,4", "-34,0", and "3,40" each have three significant digits.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: optional
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: See Clause 26.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.6 Referenced_class_identifier
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: referenced_class_identifier
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: link to an Item_class information object
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: The class referenced contains a set of Property information objects. The Property information object from which the reference is made shall have the value_format "CLASS_INSTANCE_TYPE" or "CLASS_REFERENCE_TYPE" (see 10.4.4 and 10.4.5).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: optional
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: Upper-case Latin letters "A" through "Z", except the upper-case Latin letters "O" and "I" plus digits "0" through "9".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.7 Unit_ofmeasure
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: unit_of measure
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: prescription of the unit in which the value of a property should be expressed
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Conventions and requirements:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) Preference shall be given to SI units without decimal multiplier prefixes as defined in the IEC 80000 and ISO 80000 series.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) Alternative units may be specified by using the code of the unit as specified in IEC TS 62720 or compliant unit dictionaries.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 The unit dictionaries can be supplied in computer-sensible form or as paper.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) The conversion to a different unit is outside the scope of this document.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: d) It is out of scope of this document to prescribe the use of a specific unit for transaction purposes including possible prefixes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: e) It is strongly recommended not to specify the same concept with different Property information objects if only the prefixes of the related units are different. Exceptions may occur if certain units are common in particular business domains, such as "nm" (nanometre) in semiconductor manufacturing or "kV" (kilovolt) in power distribution area.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: f) Each unit contained in the unit_ofmeasure attribute is required to be associated with a string representation, whose text representation can be used for characterizing the unit at the instance level.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 Property information objects with data_type "CLASS_REFERENCE_TYPE" do not carry a unit.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE The IRDI of unit " % " is " 0112/2///62720#UAA000#01 " $ ^{3} . $
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: conditional
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Condition: unit_of measure shall be specified for quantitative Property information objects
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of values: See Clause 26.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.8 Value_format
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute name: value_format
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definition: specification of type and length of the representation of the value of a Property
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: optional
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Character type of See Clause 26. values:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Comments
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The value_format is specified as part of a Property and can be used at implementation level for purposes of consistency and error checking in electronic exchange.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: At implementation level, e.g. in the set-up of product information databases or electronic exchange, it can be treated as a default format that can be used as-is, re-defined (restricted or extended), or ignored entirely depending on the requirements and context in which the information is used.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For Property information objects of which the data_type has the value "class_reference_type", no value_format is requested.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: See Annex G for the specification of syntax and content of value_format.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Below an overview of the content of value_format is provided:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) Non-quantitative value_format types:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A = alphabetic, letters only;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: M = mixed, all characters allowed;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: N = numeric, digits only;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: X = alphanumeric;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: B = binary, 0 or 1.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) Quantitative value_format types:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NR1 = integers;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NR2 = rational numbers with decimal-mark (real numbers);
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NR3 = rational numbers with decimal-mark and exponent-mark (floating point numbers);
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: S = signed (positive or negative numbers);
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: . = decimal-mark;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: E = exponent-mark, base 10: (A)E(B) represents the value $ A\times1 0^{B}. $
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) Field length
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The field length of a non-quantitative value shall be indicated by a number (e.g. 17). A variable field length shall start with two dots. The following preferred formats have been defined:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A fixed field length starts with one space. In such formats, no special characters shall occur.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The field length of a quantitative value shall be indicated by a combination of digits and characters (e.g. "3.3ES2"). The following preferred standard formats have been defined:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NR1 S..4
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NR3 S..3.3ES2
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A fixed field length starts with one space. In such formats no special characters shall occur.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 "NR14", "NR1S4"
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 11 Condition_property
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 11.1 Specification of information object
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Name: Condition_property
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Definition: property information object that affects the value of another property.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: Any instance of Condition_property shall contain the value "CONDITION_DET" in the (inherited) attribute product_data_element_type.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Many properties have values which depend on the value(s) of one or more additional Property information objects.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: When the value of a condition is given as a range, it shall be specified by two Condition_property information objects, representing the upper and lower bound of this range.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE Condition_property is a subtype of Property. Thus it inherits all relationships from the attribute classes of the supertype, i.e. identifying attributes, semantic attributes, administrative attributes, value attributes, and translation data.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 12.3 Property_data_element_type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 16 Value_list
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 16.1 Specification of information object
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Name: Value_list
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Definition: set of representations of permissible values of a Property
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Obligation: conditional
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Condition: Value_list shall be specified for classifying property information objects. For non-classifying property information objects a Value_list is optional.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Description: An enumeration data type always references a Value_list for specifying the set of possible values (see 10.4.3).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Value lists that form a polymorphism (see 24.7) are considered to be restrictive, because these are exhaustive and no additional or modified value is possible.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: All other value lists may be specified as being extendable by the user. For explicitly indicating the fact of having an extended value list, the option "others" shall be added to the value list in question to indicate an extended value list. The options specifying the meaning of the "others" shall be added as a condition of the property referencing the value list. This condition shall contain the additional options as an enumeration data type. In cases when the additional options are not yet specified, this enumeration remains empty.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 In this case the (original) enumeration type property is specified as DEPENDENT_P_DET. Such entries can be incorporated into the value list for a future release of the dictionary.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Property specialization as introduced in IEC 62656-1:2014, 5.4.5 is another technique for specifying properties with value lists differing from those contained in the ontology supplied by the original provider of the dictionary. This technique avoids any interference with the content delivered by the original provider.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 In cases where value lists have to be narrowed, Relation information objects can be used (see 24.8.2).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 3 In cases where a value list should be permanently extended, the value range can be extended by revising the enumeration information object in question.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE Value_list can be assigned to a Property via the attribute data_type. In case of an assigned value list this attribute contains one of the enumeration data types which include the reference to the Value_list (see 10.4.3).
layout_details.label: text

A new revision of a Drawing shall be generated if the drawing is changed without affecting either its use or its meaning, or when corrections of typing or spelling errors have been implemented.

layout_details.content: ## 19 Unit of measure
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 19.1 Overview
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Quantitative Property information objects require information about their physical quantity and the applicable unit(s). Without the unit of measure, any assigned values are meaningless and serious errors can occur.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute data_element_type_class (see 6.3) specifies the physical quantity of the Property information object. Thus preselecting suitable units is supported and the identification and assignment of the unit of measure is much simplified.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 Annex B lists use and available type classification codes of properties.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The unit of measure may be specified by using the codes specified in IEC TS 62720 or compliant unit dictionaries.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 IEC maintains in IEC CDD an IEC TS 62720 compliant collection of some 1500 units grouped as physical quantities readily available for use with Property information objects. The Property attributes code_of_unit and code_of_alternative_unit allow referencing these information objects.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Additionally, system of quantities is available through Relation and its attribute role_of_the_relation = QUANTITY (see 22.7). Thus, the existing systems of units may be implemented.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 3 Currently the system(s) of units are implemented via the IEC CDD information object "List of units" which is a predecessor of the above referenced Relation information object.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 4 Even though being designed as integral part of IEC 61360 series compliant environments, instantiated Unit of measure information objects can also be referenced via ICID from environments other than IEC 61360 series for providing unambiguous information about unit of measure.Figure 18 shows the overview model of the module "Measure concept" using UML as presentation technique.
